literal: I busy. This phrase is not idiomatic and translates directly.
usage: This is the standard, everyday way to say I am busy in Cairo. It is used in both formal and casual contexts, from workplace meetings to declining an invitation from a friend. The adjective must agree with the gender of the speaker.

variants.label: Feminine speaker
variants.note: Used when the speaker is a woman.

variants.label: Group of speakers
variants.note: Used when speaking on behalf of a group or family.

variants.label: A bit busy
variants.note: A softer way to decline an invitation or ask for time.

variants.label: Very busy
variants.note: Used to emphasize that you have absolutely no free time.

variants.label: Alternative idiom
variants.note: A common, casual alternative meaning I have things behind me (obligations).

examples.arabic: مَعْلِش، أَنَا مَشْغُول دِلْوَقْتِي. خَلِّينَا نِتْكَلِّم بَعْدِين.
examples.transliteration: ma3lesh, ana mashghoul delwaqti. khalleena netkallem ba3deen.
examples.english: Sorry, I'm busy right now. Let's talk later.

examples.arabic: مِش هَقْدَر آجي الحَفْلَة، أَنَا مَشْغُول جِدّاً فِي الشُّغْل.
examples.transliteration: mesh haqdar agi el 7afla, ana mashghoul geddan fi el shoghl.
examples.english: I can't come to the party, I'm very busy with work.

examples.arabic: إِنْتَ مَشْغُول النَّهَارْدَة وَلَّا مُمْكِن نِتْقَابِل؟
examples.transliteration: enta mashghoul el naharda walla momken netqabel?
examples.english: Are you busy today or can we meet?
